greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who stands at the door of our hearts and knocks, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the faithful and true witness: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you invite us to dine with you in your kingdom: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you seek and save what was lost: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
homily:
We begin today with a very small, very familiar image: the act of climbing. Think of a child spotting something just out of reach—a branch of a tree, a shelf, or a high ledge—and the sheer, single-minded determination that takes over. They don't worry about the dirt on their knees or the awkwardness of the scramble. They only see the goal. In today’s Gospel, we find Zacchaeus in exactly that position. He is a man of status, a chief tax collector, yet he is 'short in stature.' He cannot see over the crowd. He cannot reach the vision he craves. So, he runs ahead. He abandons his dignity and climbs a sycamore tree. He puts himself in a position to be seen. He makes himself vulnerable for the sake of a glimpse of the Truth.

I want you to hold onto this image: the climb. It is the image of a soul that refuses to be blocked by the noise of the world. It is the image of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way Benjamin approached the world. He was a boy who was always climbing—not for status, but for understanding. Whether he was diving into the complex architecture of cloud infrastructure, mastering math that reached far beyond his years, or simply looking out an airport window at a Boeing 737, he was a boy who wanted to see more. He was a boy who looked at the horizon and saw not just a distance to be traveled, but a mystery to be understood. He climbed toward knowledge, he climbed toward joy, and he climbed toward the people he loved, always with that bright, curious, and gentle spirit.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know that the calendar moves forward, but the heart often pauses in the quiet spaces where his laughter used to echo. We know the sharp, sudden ache that comes when you see something he would have loved—a new technological advancement, a bird in flight, or a moment of family joy—and the silence that follows is profound. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the waves of sorrow that ambush you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are the language of a love that is still very much alive.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together from the streets of Asia to the sacred places of Europe, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus stops beneath that sycamore tree and looks up. He doesn't see a sinner or a tax collector; he sees a man who is hungry for him. He says, 'Zacchaeus, come down quickly, for today I must stay at your house.' It is an invitation into intimacy. The crowd grumbles, as crowds often do, but Jesus ignores the noise of the world to focus on the heart of the one who sought him. This is the hinge of the mystery. Benjamin spent his life seeking. He sought connection, he sought wisdom, and he sought the joy of being with his family. And now, he is the one who has been found. He is the one who has been invited into the house of the Father. He is not lost in the distance; he is dining at the table of the Lord. He is the one who has reached the top of the climb, and he is looking down at you with a smile that is even brighter, even more peaceful, than the one you remember.

Consider the first reading from Revelation: 'Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will enter his house and dine with him, and he with me.' This is a word for you. You have been through so much. You have endured the unthinkable, and yet, you are still here, still gathering, still loving, still remembering. You have not grown weary in your love for Benjamin. You keep his memory alive in such beautiful, quiet ways. Think of the way his love continues to ripple out into the world. Think of the 'Well of Love' in Cà Mau, that clean water flowing in his name, bringing life to those who were thirsty. That is the work of a life that continues to bear fruit. That is the way Benjamin’s kindness ripples out into the world, touching the lives of people he never met, in a place he may never have walked. His life was not a brief flicker; it was a fire that continues to burn in the hearts of those who knew him.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the shared laughter, the way you both looked out the window on those train rides, the way you navigated the world together. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

We hear in the Psalm today: 'He who walks blamelessly and does justice; who thinks the truth in his heart.' This is the turn of the heart. The blessing of the Lord is not that we will never suffer, but that we will never be abandoned in our suffering. Benjamin is now resting in that promise. He is dwelling in the land of the living, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside kindred spirits, watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where Ben and his dad stood outside room 419, and Ben said with that earnest voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain overnight, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, only the clear, bright presence of God. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. He is holding the key to that reunion, and he is waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again in the house of the Father.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
petition_call: In our need, we turn to the Lord and say:
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the light of Christ and find joy in the banquet of heaven, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving, especially Benjamin's family, that the Lord may console their hearts, strengthen their spirits, and give them the peace that passes all understanding, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, heard the Lord saying to me:
“To the angel of the Church in Sardis, write this:“‘The one who has the seven spirits of God
and the seven stars says this: “I know your works,
that you have the reputation of being alive, but you are dead.
Be watchful and strengthen what is left, which is going to die,
for I have not found your works complete in the sight of my God.
Remember then how you accepted and heard; keep it, and repent.
If you are not watchful, I will come like a thief,
and you will never know at what hour I will come upon you.
However, you have a few people in Sardis
who have not soiled their garments;
they will walk with me dressed in white,
because they are worthy.“‘The victor will thus be dressed in white,
and I will never erase his name from the book of life
but will acknowledge his name in the presence of my Father
and of his angels.“‘Whoever has ears ought to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.’”“"To the angel of the Church in Laodicea, write this:“‘The Amen, the faithful and true witness,
the source of God’s creation, says this:
“I know your works;
I know that you are neither cold nor hot.
I wish you were either cold or hot.
So, because you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold,
I will spit you out of my mouth.
For you say, ‘I am rich and affluent and have no need of anything,’
and yet do not realize that you are wretched,
pitiable, poor, blind, and naked.
I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may be rich,
and white garments to put on
so that your shameful nakedness may not be exposed,
and buy ointment to smear on your eyes so that you may see.
Those whom I love, I reprove and chastise.
Be earnest, therefore, and repent.“‘Behold, I stand at the door and knock.
If anyone hears my voice and opens the door,
then I will enter his house and dine with him,
and he with me.
I will give the victor the right to sit with me on my throne,
as I myself first won the victory
and sit with my Father on his throne.“‘Whoever has ears ought to hear
what the Spirit says to the churches.’”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (Rev. 3: 21) I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
He who walks blamelessly and does justice;
who thinks the truth in his heart
and slanders not with his tongue.
R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
Who harms not his fellow man,
nor takes up a reproach against his neighbor;
By whom the reprobate is despised,
while he honors those who fear the LORD.
R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
Who lends not his money at usury
and accepts no bribe against the innocent.
He who does these things
shall never be disturbed.
R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
At that time Jesus came to Jericho and intended to pass through the town.
Now a man there named Zacchaeus,
who was a chief tax collector and also a wealthy man, 
was seeking to see who Jesus was;
but he could not see him because of the crowd,
for he was short in stature. 
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree in order to see Jesus,
who was about to pass that way.
When he reached the place, Jesus looked up and said, 
“Zacchaeus, come down quickly,
for today I must stay at your house.” 
And he came down quickly and received him with joy. 
When they saw this, they began to grumble, saying, 
“He has gone to stay at the house of a sinner.” 
But Zacchaeus stood there and said to the Lord,
“Behold, half of my possessions, Lord, I shall give to the poor,
and if I have extorted anything from anyone
I shall repay it four times over.”
And Jesus said to him,
“Today salvation has come to this house
because this man too is a descendant of Abraham. 
For the Son of Man has come to seek
and to save what was lost.”

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
